subject: GoldBank feature accelerant & commitment timeline
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GoldBank feature accelerant & commitment timeline

Team — looping you in on an ask from GoldBank that just moved from discovery to exec sign-off. Asha (GoldBank) has confirmed they will sign a multi-year commitment if we can guarantee a hard SLO for peak latency (95th < 180ms) for a set of high-throughput endpoints and provide an inspection-friendly redaction pipeline. The revenue lift is material (Ben, see attached MOP + contract sketch).

Key constraints from GoldBank:
- 24/7 peak traffic windows; latency spikes during batch runs are cause for concern.
- Need deterministic routing for a subset of calls used in fraud scoring; they want a binding playbook if latency regresses.
- Compliance team wants inline redaction and exportable audit events for each inference.

What we are asking Product/Eng: can we commit to a fast, deliverable path that we can present at the executive review next Tuesday? Monica and I discussed a phased deliverable — initial mitigations to meet the latency SLO for the top 30 intents, then follow-on work for full routing determinism and audit pipes.

Attachments: GOLDBANK_mutual_action_plan_v3.xlsx (MAP), redwood-accelerant-design-notes.pdf (sketch).

Immediate ask: short triage call today (30m) to align scope and whether we can promise a sprint slot in the next two sprints (ideally starting May 24). If full scope is too large, we need an explicit minimal scope we can promise by next Tuesday.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise GTM Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0187

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:45:22 -0700
Subject: Re: GoldBank feature accelerant & commitment timeline

Thanks Vanessa — short and to the point. Asha told me the execs have a clear gating item: either a proof we can hit the SLO for their high-frequency fraud endpoint under a 10x load test, or a commitment to a staged SLA with financial remedies. This is a $4.8M ARR expansion over 3 years if we get it.

If Product/Eng could give us a hard minimum that ensures the 95th percentile target for the top traffic slice, we can sign heads of terms in next-week's meeting. I appreciate this is a heavy ask — we should also be explicit about risk and rollback.

Ben
Enterprise AE

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:07:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: GoldBank feature accelerant & commitment timeline

Appreciate the context, Vanessa + Ben. A few clarifying questions before we scope: 
1) When you say "top 30 intents" — do you have a specific traffic histogram? (We need token length, avg latency per model, and request distribution.)
2) Deterministic routing — do they require hard affinity to a specific runtime (dedicated pool), or is a policy-based affinity (route pref + failover) acceptable for now?
3) Audit events — are they OK with a streaming audit log (export to their SIEM) or do they need deep per-request payload snapshots retained in our logs?

If we get that data today, I can sketch a phased scope by end of day with tradeoffs.

Irene
Sr. PM, Serving & Ops

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:34:50 -07:00
Subject: Re: GoldBank feature accelerant & commitment timeline

Forwarded message:
> On Fri, May 14, 2027 at 09:12, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Team — looping you in on an ask from GoldBank that just moved from discovery to exec sign-off...

Quick feasibility note from Eng: we can hit a practical, testable mitigation that reduces variance and meets a 95th < 180ms for a constrained footprint with work in two areas:
- Pre-warm shim: route-affinity + small per-customer in-memory-prefill for top N prompt templates (limited to N=20 initially). This avoids cold start jitter.
- Bounded KV caching: short-lived, request-keyed cache to reduce autoregressive KV loads for hot paths.

Estimate: 3 sprints for a narrow phased delivery (design spike + two sprints for implementation + canary). If we compress and pull a small infra task force (2 SWE, 1 infra eng, 1 SRE), we can prototype a canary in 6 weeks. Full deterministic routing (hard pin to dedicated pool) is heavier — requires infra provisioning + tenancy controls and is 10+ weeks.

Questions: Do we need inline redaction (on the serving path) or is a nearline redaction pipeline acceptable for the canary? Inline adds complexity and latency but is doable for a narrow set of fields.

I'll block time for a 30m triage today at 16:00 PT to align.

—Laura
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GoldBank feature accelerant & commitment timeline

Thanks all — Asha just replied with the traffic histogram and a terse note: they will accept a phased warranty if the initial phase guarantees the SLO for the top 25 intents accounting for their highest-volume 6-hour windows (attached in the Drive link). They explicitly prefer a route-affinity solution over dedicated pools for cost reasons, but will accept a temporary dedicated lane if we can accelerate delivery.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/GOLD-2027-EXP-42 (notes + exec emails).
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bGoldBankSprintArtifacts (traffic_histogram.csv uploaded).

Customer-facing acceptance criteria (proposed):
- 95th percentile latency < 180ms during a 10x synthetic load test for the top 25 intents.
- Fault-tolerant fallback with documented rollback steps.
- Audit events exported to their SIEM (nearline acceptable for phase 1) with schema we agree on.

If Eng can commit to the 6-week compressed canary, we can present that as a binding roadmap at exec review. If not, we need the exact number of sprints and the minimal scope we can promise so we can negotiate alternatives (e.g., temporary pricing credits).

Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GoldBank feature accelerant & commitment timeline

Follow-up from today's triage (notes below) — thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Summary we can take to execs: 

Agreed phased plan:
Phase 1 (compressed canary, 6 weeks):
- Route-affinity + pre-warm shim for top 25 intents (N=25 prompt templates).
- Short-lived request-keyed KV cache for hot paths.
- Nearline audit export to SIEM (schema v0.1).
- Load test runbook and rollback playbook documented.

Phase 2 (post-signature, 10+ weeks):
- Optional dedicated lane for deterministic routing if GoldBank chooses to fund infra carveout.
- Inline redaction for a broader set of PII fields and long-term retention policy.

Action items:
- Engineering to confirm RU allocation and node-level changes (Laura): detailed RFC by May 21 EOD.
- Product to finalize acceptance criteria and MAP updates (Irene + Monica): MAP v4 to GoldBank by May 24.
- Sales to align legal on staged SLA wording and remedies (Ben + Vanessa): draft heads of terms by May 20.

I will present this plan at the exec review on May 25 and will note the conditional nature of Phase 2. If anyone sees a blocker in the RFC timeline, flag it to me and Laura today.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise GTM Lead, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0187
